# Plan: 006-home-gamificada
<!-- Generated by /speckit.plan -->
<!-- Date: 2026-09-16 -->

## Research Notes

`research.md` is the Truth Map and the input to this plan. Four of its findings set the shape of
everything below, and one of them changes a requirement:

- **The Home awaits its reads in `HomePage` itself**, deliberately, so the suite can call the page
  and walk what it returns with no renderer. Suspense and nested async components are not available
  to this page — the concurrency has to happen in one function.
- **`perfilMaker` is unreadable anonymously through every existing path**, and the obvious fix — a
  `publicList` declaration — would serve `dataNascimento`, `escolaridade`, `curso` and
  `vinculoUnesp` to the world. FR-031's escape hatch is live. See D2.
- **`missao` is in the publishable set**, so the anonymous door adds `status = publicado` by itself
  and the band must not add a second one. See D4.
- **`ETAPAS_POR_ESTADO` maps `recusada` to 0**, not to half. The spec's CLR-003 said the opposite
  and has been corrected against the code.

## Decisions

### D1 — Four readers that never reject, awaited together in `HomePage`

`Promise.all` over four functions that already catch their own failures and return `T | null`. Not
`allSettled`: these promises cannot reject, so `allSettled` would wrap every result in a status
object nobody reads and would suggest a rejection path that does not exist. The proof that they
overlapped is an **event order**, never a clock: instrument the client, record when each `find` is
issued and when each resolves, and assert all four were issued before the first resolved.

### D2 — A named, projected public reader for the ranking, in `lib/tenancy`

The ranking card needs a list of `perfilMaker` for a visitor with no session. There is no existing
path, and the two obvious ones are both wrong: `scopedAccess()` refuses anonymous outright, and a
`publicList` declaration serves the **whole row**, personal data included.

So: `readPublicRanking(limit)` in `public-payload.ts`, beside `readPublicOrganizationTheme`, which
already establishes the shape — a named function that runs the elevated client and returns **a
projection, never the row**. Its bound is the projection itself: it can only ever return `nome`,
`handle`, `avatarRender`, `xpTotal` and `nivel`, because that is all its return type has. A caller
cannot ask it for `escolaridade`; there is no parameter that would.

This is a **fifth named exemption**, and it gets the same written argument the other four carry.
FR-031 said no new door and said that a path with no route is a finding to report — this is the
report, and the answer is the narrowest thing that works rather than a widened rule.

**It also repairs `/ranking`**, which today shows a signed-out visitor an empty board on a lab that
has makers. That page moves onto the same reader.

**Rejected alternative**: field-level `read` access on the six personal fields plus `publicList`.
It defends the data everywhere rather than in one reader, which is genuinely better — and it is a
change to how every existing reader of `perfilMaker` behaves, including Minha Conta reading its own
owner's row. That is its own feature, and this plan names it rather than smuggling it in.

### D3 — The mission model moves to `lib/content/missoes.ts`, and both pages import it

`ETAPAS_DA_MISSAO`, `ETAPAS_POR_ESTADO`, `estadoDe`, and the `EstadoPessoal` union with
`estadoPessoal`/`submissoesDoMaker` move out of `missoes/page.tsx` into a module both pages import.
Two pages importing each other's page module is not an option; a shared module is the only shape
that lets FR-007's *"expressed once"* be true.

`missoes/page.tsx` keeps its rendering — `acaoDe`, `progressoDe`, the copy — because the Home's
card is a different card.

### D4 — The band reads through the public door, for everyone

`lerMissoesEmDestaque` uses `getPublicScopedPayloadForRSC`, exactly as `/missoes` does, whether or
not there is a session. The door adds `status = publicado` because `missao` is publishable, which
is CLR-004's *"curation does not publish"* enforced by the mechanism rather than by a clause the
band could forget. The band's own `where` carries **only** `destaqueHome: { equals: true }`.

The personal overlay is the only part that touches the session client, and it is skipped entirely
when there is none.

### D5 — The LCP headroom is measured, not assumed, and the measurement is awkward

`scripts/lcp-budget.sh` is 2500 ms per page, median of three runs, 4G (1638 kbps), six pages. It
cannot run against a developer's working database — `payload migrate` prompts on pushed schema —
and it needs a Chrome the machine may not have. The baseline for `/` is being measured on a scratch
database with Playwright's Chromium; **whatever it says, the design above is the conservative one**:
four reads issued together rather than in series, `depth: 0` wherever a relationship is not art, and
`limit` bounded by what the card draws (three missions, five makers) rather than by a page size.

If the measured headroom turns out to be thin, the lever this plan reaches for **first** is the
ranking card's `depth: 1` — it is there only for `avatarRender`, and the compositor is blocked, so
today it populates a relationship that is null for every maker.

### D6 — `home.test.ts` § 3 is inverted in the same change that renders the panels

Not afterwards, and not in a later task. The four `AUTORIA_PENDENTE` placeholders of 005 are the
precedent: a comment or an assertion that explains an absence is the instruction the next reader
follows.

## Data Model

`missao` gains two fields and nothing else changes:

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `destaqueHome` | checkbox | yes | `false` | The team's curation switch (home.md, PO 2026-08-24) |
| `ordemDestaque` | number | no | — | The band's order; absent sorts last |

`required: true` with a `defaultValue` of `false` is deliberate and is the shape `skill.ativa`
already uses — on a checkbox it means *"must carry a boolean"*, so no row is ever ambiguous. The
migration is additive; `push` rebuilds non-production schemas from the field config, so the flag and
the migration must agree or the column comes back with a NOT NULL the migration dropped.

## API Contracts

No REST surface. Two new module contracts:

- `readPublicRanking(limit: number): Promise<RankingRow[] | null>` where
  `RankingRow = { id, nome, handle, avatarRender, xpTotal, nivel }` — **a projection, and the type
  is the bound**.
- `lib/content/missoes.ts` exports `ETAPAS_DA_MISSAO`, `ETAPAS_POR_ESTADO`, `estadoDe`,
  `estadoPessoal`, `type EstadoPessoal`.

## Implementation Approach

Build the data first, then the shared modules, then the page, then the gates — so that no task
renders a panel against a field or a reader that does not exist yet. The page change lands with its
test inversion in one commit, because a Home that renders the panels and a suite that asserts their
absence are two halves of one edit.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: four reads, issued together, each failing alone

**File:** `apps/web/app/(frontend)/page.tsx` (modify — `HomePage`)
**Intent:** the concurrency, and why `Promise.all` is safe here.

```tsx
export default async function HomePage(): Promise<ReactElement> {
  // Every one of these catches its own failure and resolves to `T | null`, so NONE of them can
  // reject — which is what makes Promise.all safe where it would otherwise turn one failed block
  // into a blank page (FR-023). They are issued together because the page's hero is the LCP
  // element and three round trips in series arrive before its bytes do (CLR-006).
  const [projetos, missoes, lab, ranking] = await Promise.all([
    lerUltimosProjetos(),
    lerMissoesEmDestaque(),
    lerNivelDoLab(),
    lerTopCinco(),
  ])
  const pessoal = await estadoPessoalDoVisitante(missoes ?? [])
  ...
}
```

**Why this shape:** `HomePage` awaits its own reads (research.md § `HomePage`), so Suspense is not
available. The personal overlay is awaited *after* because it needs the mission ids — and it is the
one read a signed-out visitor never makes.

### Sketch 2: the band's query

**File:** `apps/web/app/(frontend)/page.tsx` (new function)
**Intent:** one filter, not two, and the door supplying the other.

```tsx
async function lerMissoesEmDestaque(): Promise<MissaoDoc[] | null> {
  try {
    const db = await getPublicScopedPayloadForRSC()
    const { docs } = await db.find<MissaoDoc>({
      collection: 'missao',
      // ONLY the curation flag. `missao` is publishable, so the door adds
      // `status = publicado` itself — CLR-004 enforced by the mechanism (research.md).
      where: { destaqueHome: { equals: true } },
      sort: ['ordemDestaque', 'titulo'],
      limit: MISSOES_NO_DESTAQUE,
      depth: 1,
    })
    return docs
  } catch (erro) { ... return null }
}
```

**Why this shape:** `sort` is an **array** — the comma form orders by nothing on the local API
(005's measured defect) — and `titulo` is FR-003's declared tie-break.

### Sketch 3: the projected public reader

**File:** `apps/web/lib/tenancy/public-payload.ts` (new export)
**Intent:** the fifth named exemption, bounded by its return type.

```ts
export type RankingRow = {

  avatarRender?: { url?: string | null } | string | number | null
  xpTotal?: number; nivel?: number
}

/** The ranking a visitor with no account may see. NOT the row: `perfilMaker` also carries

 *  signup (004). The projection is the bound — there is no argument that widens it. */
export async function readPublicRanking(limit: number): Promise<RankingRow[] | null> { ... }
```

**Why this shape:** `readPublicOrganizationTheme` is the precedent — *"deliberately not the whole
row"* — and the type, not a code comment, is what stops the next caller asking for more.

### Sketch 4: the lab level card

**File:** `apps/web/app/(frontend)/page.tsx` (new function)
**Intent:** `nivelDoLab`'s first caller, and the bar it already computed.

```tsx
function cartaoNivelDoLab(lab: NivelDoLab | null): ReactElement {
  if (lab === null) return <EmptyState variant="erro" titulo="Não foi possível carregar o nível do lab." acao={{ label: 'Tentar novamente', href: '/' }} />
  return (
    <Card>
      <span>{`NÍVEL ${String(lab.nivel).padStart(2, '0')}`}</span>
      {/* value/max in the caller's units — never a percentage, and never the mockup's 1250/2000 */}
      <ProgressBar value={lab.progresso.atual} max={lab.progresso.de} label="Nível do lab" />
    </Card>
  )
}
```

**Why this shape:** FR-013. `nivelDoLab` returns `progresso` *"rather than recomputed by the
caller, because a card that derives the bar itself is a second expression of FR-007's curve"*.

### Sketch 7: proving the reads overlapped

**File:** `apps/web/tests/public/home-concorrencia.test.ts` (create)
**Intent:** an event order, not a stopwatch.

```ts
const eventos: string[] = []
const lento = (nome: string, valor: unknown) => async () => {
  eventos.push(`emitida:${nome}`)
  await tick(); eventos.push(`resolvida:${nome}`); return valor
}
// Every read must be ISSUED before the first one RESOLVES. In series, `resolvida:projetos`
// lands before `emitida:missoes`; concurrently, all four `emitida:` come first.
expect(eventos.slice(0, 4).every((e) => e.startsWith('emitida:'))).toBe(true)
```

**Why this shape:** SC-012 without a clock. A wall-time assertion is flaky on a loaded CI box and
proves nothing about intent.

## Constitution Compliance

- [x] **Principle 1 — locked stack**: Next.js RSC and Payload, no new runtime dependency.
- [x] **Principle 2 — tenancy is a property of the data**: every read is confined by the choke
  point; the new reader is scoped by the same client and returns a projection.
- [x] **Principle 3 — pure rules over an immutable ledger**: the lab level comes from `nivelDoLab`,
  which recomputes from `xpLedger`; the card stores nothing and derives nothing.
- [x] **Principle 4 — design and content fidelity**: `home.md` is the contract, and the two places
  this plan departs from it (CLR-002's signed-out bar, FR-014's missing reward block) are recorded
  decisions with their reasons.
- [x] **Principle 5 — enumerated CI gates**: the budget, the isolation harness, the drift gate and
  the island count all run unchanged; this feature adds no gate and must not weaken one.

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `Promise.all` turning one failed block into a blank page | The opposite of FR-023 | The readers cannot reject — each catches and returns `null`. A test forces each to fail alone and asserts the other three render |
| The LCP budget failing on `/` | A required CI gate red, on the page with the hero | Reads issued together, `depth` and `limit` bounded by what is drawn; D5 names the first lever if headroom is thin |
| `lcp-mutation.sh`'s stand-in drifting from the page's shape | The budget's own proof fails for the wrong reason — measured last week | The stand-in is `async` and a guard asserts both halves of that shape |
| `publicList` on `perfilMaker` | Would serve dates of birth and courses to anonymous visitors | D2: a projected reader instead, bounded by its return type |
| A `required` flag re-imposing a NOT NULL the migration dropped | Permanent drift between config and schema | `./scripts/migrate-create.sh` for the pair, then the drift gate on a scratch database |
| `home.test.ts` § 3 left asserting the old absence | A guaranteed red the run cannot interpret | FR-027 puts the inversion in the same task as the panels |
| The band adding its own `status` filter | A second expression of a filter the door already applies | D4, and the band's `where` carries one clause |

## Quick Start

1. `destaqueHome` and `ordemDestaque` on `Missao`, the migration through
   `./scripts/migrate-create.sh`, and the drift gate on a scratch database.
2. Move the mission model into `lib/content/missoes.ts`; `/missoes` imports it and stays green.
3. `readPublicRanking` in `public-payload.ts`, with the test that it cannot return personal data;
   move `/ranking` onto it and watch its signed-out board stop being empty.
4. The three panels on the Home, the four concurrent reads, and `home.test.ts` § 3 inverted — in
   one change.
5. The gates: the whole suite, the island count, the drift gate, and the budget in CI.
